references.text: The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to inhabited land. This shows how God provided food for the people in the wilderness without ordinary bread.
The Nazirites' abstention from wine and strong drink as a sign of consecration to the Lord, parallel to Israel's abstinence in the wilderness.
God humbled the people and let them hunger, but gave them manna to teach them that man does not live by bread alone. The same theme of God's care and instruction in the wilderness.
God gave them manna in the wilderness, which their fathers did not know. This confirms the supernatural provision that replaced ordinary food.
Their clothes did not wear out and their shoes were not worn out for forty years. Part of the same speech showing God's total care in the wilderness.
David mentions that he ate the showbread when he was hungry. Shows that God can provide outside normal means when necessary.
Jesus quotes from Deuteronomy 8:3 that man does not live by bread alone. The same teaching about dependence on God's word rather than physical food.
